validated_issues.original_description: Logic error in quat-from-euler: the 'y' component calculation uses '(* sr sp sy)' which is a typo for '(* sr cp sy)'. This results in incorrect quaternion values for ZYX Euler rotations.
validated_issues.reasoning: The formula in the source file correctly implements the ZYX Euler convention. The 'y' component already uses (* sr cp sy) as part of (+ (* cr sp cy) (* sr cp sy)). The QA agent seems to have hallucinated the presence of the typo.

validated_issues.original_description: The quat-slerp function performs two redundant calls to quat-dot for the same pair of quaternions, which is inefficient for a performance-critical interpolation routine.
validated_issues.reasoning: The code calls (quat-dot a b) on line 195 and again on line 198, even though the result could be reused.

validated_issues.original_description: Hardcoded PI literal (3.141592653589793) used in quat-to-euler instead of a global constant, which is inconsistent with Core library standards.
validated_issues.reasoning: Confirmed. core/base/prelude.ss defines the constant π, which should be used instead of the literal for consistency and precision.

validated_issues.original_description: Deflation logic in qr-algorithm-shifted-loop is flawed. It reduces the 'active-size' for shift calculation but continues to perform QR decomposition on the full-sized matrix. This negates the performance benefits of deflation and can introduce numerical noise into already converged eigenvalues.
validated_issues.reasoning: Confirmed. The loop passes the full matrix to matrix-qr and matrix-mul regardless of the active-size, leading to O(N^3) work per iteration even when sub-matrices have converged.

validated_issues.original_description: The eigen-decomposition function uses unit vectors as a fallback when inverse iteration fails to converge. This is mathematically incorrect as unit vectors are not eigenvectors of general matrices.
validated_issues.reasoning: Confirmed. Setting a column to a unit vector in the eigenvector matrix when convergence fails is mathematically invalid and hides computation errors.

validated_issues.original_description: wilkinson-shift lacks a guard for the case where d=0 and discriminant < 0 for non-symmetric matrices, potentially leading to a division by zero if tolerance is very small.
validated_issues.reasoning: The code includes a guard (if (< denom *eigen-tolerance*) a-ii ...) which handles the case where denom is zero or near-zero, preventing the division by zero.

validated_issues.original_description: d-pow implementation lacks handling for negative exponents (n < 0), which will result in infinite recursion and a stack overflow.
validated_issues.reasoning: The implementation explicitly handles negative exponents on lines 159-161 using the reciprocal of the positive power: (d/ (lift 1) (d-pow inst x (- n))).

validated_issues.original_description: derivative-at relies on hardcoded list indexing (cadr) of the resolution result. This is brittle and will fail if the instance database order changes or if resolution returns a decorated result.
validated_issues.reasoning: Confirmed. The code assumes (resolve-differentiable 'Dual) always returns an 'ok' status and that the evidence is always at the second position without checking the status.

validated_issues.original_description: normalize-signal does not check for empty vectors, leading to a division by zero error when calculating the mean for a signal of length zero.
validated_issues.reasoning: Confirmed. If vector-length is 0, the expression (/ sum n) results in division by zero.

validated_issues.original_description: find-peaks uses non-strict inequalities (>=) for neighbor comparisons. In the presence of a plateau in the signal, it will return multiple indices for the same peak instead of a single peak or the plateau center.
validated_issues.reasoning: Confirmed. Using >= will tag every point on a plateau above the threshold as a peak, which is generally incorrect for peak detection algorithms.

gaps_found.description: Logic error: qr-algorithm-shifted-loop uses the 'identity' function (from prelude.ss, returns its argument) instead of 'matrix-identity' (which creates an identity matrix). This will cause a crash as it tries to scale an integer as if it were a matrix.

Inefficient shift implementation: creates a full N*N identity matrix in every iteration of the shifted QR loop. This should be optimized by directly updating the diagonal or using a scaled identity subtraction.
quat-from-axis-angle does not normalize the input axis. While the docstring assumes a unit vector, failure to normalize leads to non-unit quaternions, breaking subsequent rotation logic.
find-peaks ignores signal boundaries (indices 0 and n-1). If the global maximum is at the start or end of the vector, it will not be detected.

summary.notes: The original report had several hallucinations (quat-from-euler typo and d-pow negative handling), but correctly identified critical performance and safety issues. The most significant gap found was the use of the identity function instead of a matrix constructor in matrix-eigen.ss.
